newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia labour reform aids lower rates-govt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia labour reform aids lower rates-govt.

text.p: The Australian government said on Monday its labour reforms would help pave the way for lower interest rates as part of its overall economic improvement package.

"I think the more general point from the government's perspective is that we have been working very hard to improve the overall economic climate, which can pave the way for a lower interest rate regime," Australian Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.

"Certainly, the steps that the government has taken to tighten fiscal policy, to cut government spending, to cut out waste -- all of those measures, I think, pave the way for a more benign monetary policy application by the Reserve Bank."
The chances of an Australian interest rate cut were boosted last last Thursday by data thaat showed annual wages growth falling to 3.5 percent in August from 3.7 percent in May.

The wages news came one day after data showed annual headline inflation falling to 2.1 percent, its lowest level in two years, and the key underlying inflation rate falling below three percent for the first time in over a year.
The Reserve Bank of Australia last cut its official cash rate on July 31, by a half a percentage point to 7.0 percent.

Reith announced on Sunday that the government had secured passage of its Workplace Relations Bill through an agreement with the Australian Democrats under which 171 amendments will be made to the bill.
